subject: C-suite value memo, risk triage & procurement ladder for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.malhotra@mednova.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@mednova.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: C-suite value memo, risk triage & procurement ladder for Redwood pilot

Hi Rajiv / Claire —

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned before we loop in procurement and legal:

Top business goals you shared
- Reduce per-query inference cost for clinical summarization workflows by ~40% while keeping sub-200ms p99 latency for live triage scenarios.
- Avoid model lock-in: want a clear path to swap models or run on private infra later.
- Short pilot (6–8 weeks) that proves cost + latency improvements on a representative subset of patient notes.

Key pain / risks we heard
- Data residency and PHI handling in pilot (on-prem or VPC required for full dataset).
- Procurement wants a small PO / pilot contract and clear exit criteria.
- Ops need visibility into token-level costs and fallbacks for high-load periods.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot
- 6-week pilot plan: baseline metrics, two optimization waves (quantization + batching), and a runbook for fallback to smaller model variants.
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 Type II summary, sample logging schema, and a short pilot test plan.
- Exec one-pager (attached) that ties outcomes to clinical KPIs and cost savings.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the internal sponsor for procurement (name & email) so we can route the pilot SOW?
2) Will the pilot use de-identified notes first, or do we need an on-prem/VPC environment for live PHI from day one?
3) Suggest a 30-minute procurement + legal checkpoint next week; what windows work for Claire / Sanjay?

I’ve attached the one-pager, SOC2 summary, and a draft pilot test plan for your review. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm the procurement contact.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference, predictable economics

Attachments: 20261206-grace-mednova-value-memo.pdf; SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf; pilot-test-plan.xlsx

Grace —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick replies inline:
- Procurement sponsor: Sanjay Patel (sanjay.patel@mednova.com) — I’ve copied him on this thread.
- For the pilot we prefer to start with de-identified notes. If the pilot demonstrates the right latency/cost, we will scope an on-prem/VPC phase for production.
- Claire and I are available Wed/Thu morning next week for a procurement sync.

One more ask from my side: can you include a short SLA summary (uptime, latency objectives, and escalation contact) in the next note? I want to make sure our CTO has something concise for the exec packet.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director, Clinical Data Platforms
MedNova Health

Rajiv / Grace —

Adding a quick technical note and a proposed minimal validation plan you can share with CTO:
- SLA summary (short): target uptime 99.5% for hosted pilot; p95 latency <120ms, p99 <200ms on our curated model profile. Full SLA language comes with Dedicated contract.
- Data handling: pilot on de-identified data uses hosted API with strict token redaction + audit logs. For PHI, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — we can scope within procurement.
- Minimal validation tests (attached pilot-test-plan.xlsx):
  * Baseline run with 2k notes (latency + cost)
  * 2 optimization waves: (1) batching + KV cache; (2) int8 quantized variant validation
  * End-of-pilot business check: % reduction in tokens/cost and median latency improvements vs baseline

I uploaded the one-pager and test plan here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MedNova-Pilot

If you want, I can join the procurement call and walk through validation & rollback triggers.

—Jonas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Hi all —

Thanks for the summary. A couple procurement/legal questions before we run a small PO:
1) Data residency — if we move to PHI later, will Redwood support a VPC deployment in AWS us-east-1? Any lift & shift cost assumptions?
2) Liability / indemnity — need pointer to standard Redwood redlines. We typically run vendor contracts through our counsel (I will share a mark).
3) SLAs & credits — we want a concise table for uptime/latency and the credit schedule. Is there a templated SLA you can attach?

If you can provide a short answers doc and the one-pager updated with the SLA bullets, we can circulate internally and get back to you with a PO for the pilot. Otherwise, propose a Wed 10:00am ET procurement sync.

Sanjay Patel
Sr. Manager, Strategic Sourcing | MedNova Health

Appreciate the quick turn. Attached is a condensed SLA summary and answers to your procurement questions:
- VPC/on-prem: yes, Redwood Private supports AWS us-east-1. We will include estimated lift & shift engineering days in the SOW; conservative estimate is 3–5 engineering days for standard connectors (we'll refine after an infra call).
- Liability: I attached our standard liability/redline guidance doc; happy to receive your counsel’s markups.
- SLA table (attached): uptime, latency targets and a simple credit schedule for pilot tiers.

Next steps
1) Grace to send draft pilot SOW + small PO template by EOD Thu.
2) Jonas to join Wed 10:00am ET procurement sync to walk validation & rollback triggers.
3) Rajiv to share internal exec packet with CTO; we will provide the one-pager + SLA table for inclusion.

I’ll send the SOW and calendar invite now. Thanks — looking forward to getting this into motion.

Best,
